# Case test bed v1 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A parametric Blender model of the v1 case test bed (printed camera module on a rail, plus the plywood corridor it mounts on), exported as printable STLs that slice cleanly on a Bambu P1S in PETG.

**Architecture:** All geometry is generated by Python scripts that run inside Blender 5.2 (headless for builds and checks, or through the Blender MCP for the live scene). One pure-Python `params.py` holds every dimension and the camera kinematics, so the numbers are unit-tested on the host without Blender. Each printable part is one module with `build(p) -> Object`; `assembly.py` places them with the corridor and component placeholders; `verify.py` checks fit, interference, field of view and metal clearance; `slice_check.py` slices every STL with the Bambu Studio CLI.

**Tech Stack:** Blender 5.2 `bpy`/`bmesh` (Boolean modifier, Manifold solver), Python 3 stdlib (`unittest`), Bambu Studio CLI (P1S 0.4 nozzle, 0.16 mm, PETG Basic).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-case-testbed-design.md` (English translation of the approved Hungarian design `2026-11-05-tok-tesztpad-design.md`).

## Global Constraints

- Units: millimetres everywhere; Blender scene Metric, unit scale 0.001, length mm.
- World frame: X across the corridor (0 = centre), Y along it (0 = inner face of the front wall, +Y towards the entrance), Z up (0 = top of the floor board).
- Printer: Bambu Lab P1S, 0.4 nozzle, bed 256 x 256; every part must fit 250 x 250 x 250 in its print orientation, lie on Z = 0, and print without supports.
- Material PETG; walls >= 2.4 mm (6 lines at 0.4); sliding fits 0.3 mm clearance per side, press fits 0.1 mm, unless `params.py` says otherwise.
- No metal (screws, nuts, foil) within 100 mm of the antenna radiator; the antenna holder uses M4 nylon bolts and wing nuts.
- Only BLE starts a visit: no PIR mount anywhere.
- English only in code, comments and docs (repo rule). No vendor CAD from `hardware/case/ref/` in the repo; placeholders use `DIMENSIONS.md` values.
- Generated files: `hardware/case/stl/<part>.stl`, `hardware/case/station-case.blend`; they are rebuilt by `build.py`, never edited by hand.
- Blender runs through `hardware/case/cad/blender.sh <script> [args]` (env `BLENDER` overrides the binary path); every local run is wrapped in `dev-budget run --kind heavy --`.

## Review Focus

1. Tilt at 45 deg in the top rail position: the module must not hit the wall, the carriage or the rail, and the window frame must still slide out upwards. Pinned by `verify.py` interference and frame-removal checks over all 12 states (Task 7).
2. A bowl of a different size: changing `bowl_d_base` must rebuild the holder and still fit the bed, or fail `check_part.py` with a clear message (Task 5).
3. Lens behind the wall plane: at no state may the lens or window be at Y >= -12 (wall outer face) minus 3 mm standoff (Task 1 test, Task 7 check).
4. Camera cable and USB plug: the board stack, camera, USB-C overmould and LED strips must sit inside the module without touching its walls (Task 7 placeholder-interference check).
5. Antenna cable length: the u.FL route from the module to the antenna must be computed, not assumed; the spec's 15-20 cm figure is checked against it and reported (Task 1 test, README BOM).

## Decided geometry (all in `params.py`)

Corridor (plywood, not printed): `t_wood = 12`, inner `250 W x 400 H x 650 L`, dead end at the front wall. Front-wall opening `open_w = 100` (X +-50), `open_z0 = 30`, `open_z1 = 355`.

Bowl and hen: `bowl_d_top = 180`, `bowl_d_base = 150`, `bowl_h = 60` (placeholders until measured), bowl centre `bowl_y = 185`. Head placeholder: sphere D50 at `(0, bowl_y, bowl_h + 40)`.

Module local frame: origin at the tilt pivot; `x` across, `y` forward (towards the wall), `z` up. Tilt is nose-down, positive degrees, steps `TILTS = (0, 15, 30, 45)`; world placement = rotate about X by `-tilt`, then translate to `(0, pivot_y, pivot_z)`.
- `pivot_y = -23.5` (world). Rail states `RAIL_PIVOT_Z = {"low": 125, "mid": 220, "high": 315}`.
- Module body box: `x +-32`, `y +2 .. -42`, `z +6 .. -72` (64 x 44 x 78), wall `2.4`.
- Lens front at local `(0, +1, -20)`; lens bore D6.6 with an inner 45 deg entry chamfer; shroud ring D10 OD standing `2.0` proud of the front face.
- Window frame: `56 W x 40 H x 4 D`, slides down into two guides on the body front from above; top at local `z = +4`; frame front face at local `y = +6` (world -17.5 at tilt 0). Clear 20 x 20 x 2 acrylic pane over the lens; the LED windows are 0.48 mm printed PETG skins (diffuser).
- LED pockets: two vertical `9 x 26 x 2.5` pockets in the body front at `x = +-18`, centred on the lens height.
- Board stack (XIAO + Sense, length axis vertical, u.FL end up, USB-C down): main PCB back at local `y = -14`, board spans `z -12 .. -33`; USB-C overmould `12.4 x 6.5 x 25` below it; camera module 8 x 8 behind the lens.
- Board sled: slides in from the rear along `-y` on side ribs; carries the board on its front face (`y -14`) and the AO3400 perfboard `20 x 30` on its rear face.
- Pivot: M4 self-tapping screw through each carriage cheek into a module side boss at local `(+-32, 0, 0)`; index: M3 self-tapping screw through one of four cheek holes into a module boss at radius 16 behind the pivot (`(+-32, -16, 0)` at tilt 0); cheek holes at `(-16 cos theta, +16 sin theta)` for theta in `TILTS`.
- Openings: bottom rectangular hole for the USB-C overmould (13.5 x 7.5, unplug before removing the sled), top slot 3 wide for the u.FL extension, open to the rear edge and closed by the lid. Bottom vent slots; lid vent slots under an outside hood. Silica gel pocket `30 x 20 x 10` on the lid inner face. Lid fixed by 2 x M3 self-tapping screws. A zip-tie anchor bar under the body bottom, behind the USB hole, is the strain relief; the drip loop hangs below it.

Rails (two, on the front-wall outer face): centre `x = +-56`, `24 W x 9 D`, Y -12 .. -21; hex-head channel on the wall side `8.4 W x 4.5 D` (stops the M5 hex head turning), slot `5.5` through the front skin; slot Z `81.5 .. 278.5`; total length <= 250 with a countersunk 4 mm wood-screw hole in each foot; 10 mm tick marks engraved on the front face. Printed front face down.

Carriage: a frame plate Y -21 .. -27, X +-68, Z `pivot -84 .. pivot +16`, with a hole for the module between two cheeks (X +-33 .. +-39, Y -17 .. -44, Z `pivot -8 .. +18`); one M5 bolt per rail at Z `pivot - 40`, wing nut on the -Y face; a 5 x 2 guide tongue on the rail-facing side runs in each rail slot.

Bowl holder: ring inner D `bowl_d_base + 2`, wall 4, height 20, three tabs with D4.5 holes. Antenna holder: plate `130 (Y) x 50 (X) x 4`, underside pocket `38 x 18 x 1.2` for the FPC radiator, coax groove, two `4.5 x 100` slots for M4 nylon bolts; default antenna centre world `(0, 300, 400)`. Cable clip: `20 x 12 x 6`, 2 mm coax channel, one D4.5 hole (x3).

### Revised in Task 1 (authoritative: `hardware/case/cad/params.py`)

The pivot hole needed 3 mm of wall ahead of it, so the module moved forward in its own frame: body `y +5 .. -39`, lens front `(0, +4, -20)`, main PCB back `y -11`, sled ribs `y -10.8 .. -13.2`, shroud 1.5 proud, cheeks `y +8 .. -20.5`. Where this section and the one above differ, this one wins.

Window frame and guides (shared by Task 3 and Task 4, exact):
- Frame: `x +-28`, `y +5 .. +9`, `z +4 .. -38`. Grip tab `x +-6`, `y +5 .. +7`, `z +4 .. +8`.
- Pane pocket, open to the back: `x +-10.1`, `z -20 +- 10.1`, `y +5 .. +8.5`; the pane sits at `y +6.5 .. +8.5` and touches the shroud top; front aperture `x +-9`, `z -20 +- 9`.
- LED windows: `x +-18 +- 4.5`, `z -20 +- 13`, cut from the back to `y = 9 - 0.48`.
- Guides on the body: `|x| 28.3 .. 31.3`, `y +5 .. +10.5`, `z -38.3 .. +4`; lip `|x| 26.5 .. 31.3`, `y +9.3 .. +10.5`; bottom stop `x +-31.3`, `y +5 .. +9.3`, `z -40.3 .. -38.3`. The guides end at `z +4`, not at the body top: at 45 deg tilt anything higher touches the wall.
- The frame slides out upwards at tilts 0 and 15; at 30 and 45 the operator first sets the tilt to 0 (one index screw).

### Revised in Task 7 (authoritative: `hardware/case/cad/params.py` and the part modules)

Where this section and the ones above differ, this one wins.

- Carriage tongue `tongue_len = 18`; rail slot Z `73.5 .. 286.5`; `rail_foot = 18` (rail length 249).
- Front-wall opening `open_w = 80`, `open_z1 = 375` (was 100 and 355): 16 mm of wood stays beside the rail screws, and the window frame lifts out at the high rail position at tilt 15.
- Window frame grip tab height `grip z = 3.5` (1 mm wall standoff at 45 deg).
- The carriage has no top bar: the module ties the cheeks together through the pivot screws. It prints upright, Z up, on its bottom bar.
- Print orientations: module body top face down (front face down cannot work, the guides stand proud); lid outer face down, with 45 deg louvres instead of an outside hood; board sled bottom edge down, plate upright.

### Task 1: Parameters, kinematics and Blender plumbing

**Files:**
- Create: `hardware/case/cad/params.py`, `hardware/case/cad/test_params.py`, `hardware/case/cad/mesh.py`, `hardware/case/cad/blender.sh`, `hardware/case/cad/check_part.py`, `hardware/case/cad/parts/__init__.py`
- Modify: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (one step in `python-tests`)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces (`params.py`, no `bpy`): `P` frozen dataclass with the values above; `TILTS`, `RAIL_PIVOT_Z`; `lens_pose(p, pivot_z: float, tilt: float) -> tuple[Vec3, Vec3]` (lens world position, unit view direction); `local_to_world(p, pt: Vec3, pivot_z, tilt) -> Vec3`; `aim_tilt(p, pivot_z) -> float` (exact angle to the head); `nearest_tilt(angle) -> int` (from `TILTS`); `vfov_deg(p) -> float` (from 85 deg H, 4:3); `head_in_fov(p, pivot_z, tilt) -> bool` (whole head sphere inside the frustum); `antenna_cable_mm(p, pivot_z) -> float` (module top -> roof outside the wall -> roof hole -> antenna, +50 slack); `rail_length(p) -> float`.
- Produces (`mesh.py`, `bpy`): `box(name, size, center)`, `cyl(name, d, h, center, axis="Z", segments=64)`, `cone(name, d1, d2, h, center)`, `union(target, *others)`, `cut(target, *others)`, `intersect(target, other)` (all apply a Manifold Boolean modifier and delete the tools), `apply_print_rotation(obj, deg_xyz)` (rotates and drops min Z to 0), `export_stl(obj, path)`, `non_manifold_edges(obj) -> int`, `volume(obj) -> float`, `bbox(obj) -> (min, max)`, `reset_scene()`.
- Produces (`parts/__init__.py`): `PARTS = ["rail", "carriage", "module_body", "module_lid", "board_sled", "window_frame", "bowl_holder", "antenna_holder", "cable_clip"]` and `load(name)` (importlib). Each part module exposes `build(p) -> Object` (local/assembly frame), `PRINT_ROT: tuple[float, float, float]`, `COUNT: int`, optional `checks(obj, p) -> list[str]`.
- Produces (`check_part.py`): `blender.sh check_part.py <name>` builds the part, applies `PRINT_ROT`, and fails with exit 1 unless non-manifold edges = 0, volume > 0, bbox <= 2503 with min Z = 0, and `checks()` returns no errors.
